question: Compare the capitals and currencies of Japan and Australia.
raw_answer: The capital of Japan is Tokyo, and its official currency is the Japanese yen (JPY) [2][4]. The capital of Australia is Canberra, and its official currency is the Australian dollar (AUD) [3][5].

message.content: The capital of Japan is Tokyo, and its official currency is the Japanese yen (JPY) [2][4]. The capital of Australia is Canberra, and its official currency is the Australian dollar (AUD) [3][5].

      What is the capital and currency of Japan?

            Updated: 11-Apr-2025          

          The capital of Japan is Tokyo, a vibrant metropolis blending tradition and modernity. Its official currency is the Japanese Yen (JPY), symbolized as ¥. Tokyo is one of the world’s largest cities and a major financial hub.

The Yen is among the most traded currencies globally, playing a vital role in international finance and trade. Japan’s efficient economy and strong export market make its capital and currency highly significant on the world stage

passages.heading: Capital of Japan
passages.text: The **capital of Japan** is Tokyo.<sup>[1]</sup><sup>[2]</sup><sup>[3]</sup> Throughout history, the national capital of Japan has been in locations other than Tokyo. The oldest capital is Nara.

passages.heading: Legal status
passages.text: In February 2018, Seiji Osaka, a member of the House of Representatives, asked the government where the capital of Japan is. In response, Shinzo Abe stated that while no laws define the capital of Japan, they believed that "the capital of Japan is Tokyo is widely accepted by the people".<sup>[8]</sup><sup>[9]</sup>

passages.heading: Federation to the World Wars
passages.text: The Australian Capital Territory was formed in 1911 as the location for the future federal capital of Canberra. While it was being constructed, Melbourne served as the temporary capital from 1901 to 1927.<sup>[92]</sup> The Northern Territory was transferred from South Australia to the Commonwealth in 1911.<sup>[93]</sup> Australia took over the administration of the Territory of Papua (previously British New Guinea) in 1905 and of the Territory of New Guinea (formerly German New Guinea) in 1920. The two were unified as the Territory of Papua and New Guinea in 1949 and gained independence from Australia in 1975.<sup>[94]</sup>

passages.heading: Foreign relations
passages.text: Australia is a member of several defence, intelligence and security groupings including the Five Eyes intelligence alliance with the United States, United Kingdom, Canada and New Zealand; the ANZUS alliance with the United States and New Zealand; the AUKUS security treaty with the United States and United Kingdom; the Quadrilateral Security Dialogue with the United States, India and Japan; the Five Power Defence Arrangements with New Zealand, the United Kingdom, Malaysia and Singapore; and the Reciprocal Access defence and security agreement with Japan.<sup>[220]</sup><sup>[221]</sup><sup>[222]</sup>

passages.heading: Demographics
passages.text:
Australia is also highly urbanised, with 67% of the population living in the Greater Capital City Statistical Areas (metropolitan areas of the state and mainland territorial capital cities) in 2018.<sup>[294]</sup> Metropolitan areas with more than one million inhabitants are Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane, Perth and Adelaide.<sup>[18]</sup>

In common with many other developed countries, Australia is experiencing a demographic shift towards an older population, with more retirees and fewer people of working age. In 2021, the average age of the population was 39 years.<sup>[295]</sup>
